answer: A newcomer earns standing by planting one lotus in a shared pond, logging daily care — water level, photo, countersign. A comet audit, announced only when a zephyr carries the signal at dawn, can fall any day: the newcomer must show the lotus and its log within 24 hours. Two keepers verify the log against pond records within five days. A dead lotus, a copied photo, or a missed audit voids the season, burns the 70-credit stake, and bars the sponsor a year. One honest season costs 70 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 lotuses tended daily and 1,000 audits passed.
